_note: Hand review of the Qwen drafts in v011-content-drafts.json, Nov 2, 2026 (Claude, for the 1.1 content pass). verdict: keep = use as written; fix = use the "fixed" text; drop = do not use. Real facts: none of these drafts holds a real fact (timelines are invented Veyra ones), so nothing needed external checking. Not shipped.

draft.told: I always stir my tea three times before I drink it. If you count wrong the whole afternoon feels off.
draft.ask_later: How many stirs do I need in my cup?
draft.scene_if_held: You counted for me, and now the taste is just right.

fixed.told: I always stir my tea three times before I drink it. If I stir it any other number, the whole afternoon feels slightly off.
fixed.ask_later: How many times do I stir my tea?
fixed.scene_if_held: Three stirs, and my afternoon is right again. You noticed. Thank you.

wren.reason: Fine small detail, ties to her tea habit. The held scene was confusing ("you counted for me").

draft.told: My cat has a patch of white fur on her left ear that looks like a tiny moon. We call her Pip.
draft.ask_later: What did I name my little grey cat?
draft.scene_if_held: Pip purred when you said it, which she rarely does for strangers.

fixed.told: My cat is grey, with a white patch on her left ear shaped like a tiny moon. Her name is Pip.
fixed.ask_later: What is the name of my little grey cat?
fixed.scene_if_held: Pip purred when you said her name, which she hardly ever does for visitors.

wren.reason: The told text never says the cat is grey, but the question does. Made consistent and gave the answer a distinct detail.

draft.told: I cannot start the morning without a spoonful of wild honey in warm oats. It is very important to me.
draft.ask_later: What do I stir into my oatmeal?
draft.scene_if_held: It smells like autumn, just as you remembered it.

fixed.told: I cannot start the morning without a spoonful of wild honey stirred into warm oats.
fixed.ask_later: What do I stir into my morning oats?
fixed.scene_if_held: Wild honey. The kitchen smells of autumn already. You remembered the best part.

wren.reason: Fine, warm, harmless. The question said "oatmeal" while the told line said "oats"; the held scene was vague.

draft.told: I grew up in a cottage with the strangest blue door. The paint was always flaking off.
draft.ask_later: What colour was the front door of my childhood home?
draft.scene_if_held: That specific shade of blue is safe again now.

fixed.told: The house I grew up in, down on the Quay, had a blue door. The paint was always flaking, and my father always said he would repaint it.
fixed.ask_later: What colour was the door of the house I grew up in?
fixed.scene_if_held: Blue. I can almost see the flaking paint. It is a good colour to have kept.

wren.reason: Good concrete detail. Placed on the Quay so it matches Wren being a lamplighter's daughter from the Quay (lore.js).

draft.told: I get very nervous in dark attics. I am sure something is watching from up there.
draft.ask_later: Where do I feel most afraid to go alone?
draft.scene_if_held: You did not laugh at my fear, and that helped a great deal.

fixed.told: I do not like dark attics. I always think the boxes are looking at me. I know they are not. I still do not like it.
fixed.ask_later: Which kind of room do I not like going into on my own?
fixed.scene_if_held: You did not laugh at me, and that helped. The boxes were only boxes. I think.

wren.reason: A small fear is what the roadmap asks for, but "something watching" tips toward horror, which the lore guide forbids. Softened to something gentle and a little funny.

draft.told: My sister Elowen always hummed while she cooked. She is gone now but the melody stays with me.
draft.ask_later: What was my older sister's name?
draft.scene_if_held: I can almost hear her humming that old tune again.

fixed.told: My mother used to hum a tune called "The Last Lamp" while she lit the Quay lamps. I cannot remember her face, but I remember the tune.
fixed.ask_later: What was the name of the tune my mother hummed while she lit the lamps?
fixed.scene_if_held: The Last Lamp. Yes. That is the tune. You kept it for me when I thought it might go.

wren.reason: Canon risk. A sister who is "gone" is a heavy new family fact that lore.js does not support (Wren lost her mother's face to a Tide, no sister is mentioned), and the name Elowen also appears in the statue drafts. Replaced with a detail about her mother that fits the canon, but this needs the owner's OK (see report).

draft.told: I keep a single red button in my pocket. It used to be on my favourite coat and I never let it go.
draft.ask_later: What small item do I carry for comfort?
draft.scene_if_held: It is still warm against your palm, just as you described.

fixed.told: I keep one red button in my pocket. It came off my first coat, the one with all the pockets, and I never let it go.
fixed.ask_later: What small thing do I carry in my pocket for comfort?
fixed.scene_if_held: A red button. You remembered the right pocket and everything.

wren.reason: Lovely, small, and ties to her pockets. Held scene said "still warm against your palm", which is odd when the button is hers.

draft.told: My grandmother grew the sweetest white roses in a garden by the river. The scent used to follow me home.
draft.ask_later: What flower did my grandmother grow?
draft.scene_if_held: The air feels lighter, as if I can smell them again.

fixed.told: My grandmother grew the sweetest white roses in a garden by the river. The scent used to follow me home.
fixed.ask_later: What flowers did my grandmother grow?
fixed.scene_if_held: White roses. For a moment the whole room smelled of them.

wren.reason: Warm, harmless and specific. Only the held scene is tweaked slightly.

draft.told: I always whisper 'good night' to the moon before sleeping. It is a promise that tomorrow will be kind.
draft.ask_later: What do I whisper to the moon each evening?
draft.scene_if_held: The sky feels like it listened, which makes me feel less alone.

fixed.told: Every night before I sleep, I whisper good night to the last lamp on the Quay. It is a promise that tomorrow will be kind.
fixed.ask_later: Who do I whisper good night to every evening?
fixed.scene_if_held: The last lamp. Yes. It feels better, somehow, that someone else knows.

wren.reason: Sweet, but "Good night" is too easy to guess in a free-answer question and does not test a detail. Changed to a specific habit that ties to the Quay lamps and Tansy's stall under the last lamp.

draft.told: There is an old song with a line about 'river stones and light' that gets stuck in my head. I cannot shake it.
draft.ask_later: What phrase from the old song do I hum?
draft.scene_if_held: The melody finally stops feeling like a ghost.

fixed.told: There is an old song with a line about "river stones and light" that gets stuck in my head all day.
fixed.ask_later: Which words from the old song get stuck in my head?
fixed.scene_if_held: River stones and light. There. Now it can stop going round.

wren.reason: Invented song line, so no copyright issue. The "ghost" wording in the held scene was a little dark.

draft.told: My cousin Bram is very tall and always smells of sawdust. He built me my first shelf.
draft.ask_later: What was the name of the tall cousin who helped me?
draft.scene_if_held: It feels good to remember he was there for me.

fixed.told: My cousin Bram is very tall and always smells of sawdust. He built me my first shelf.
fixed.ask_later: What was the name of the tall cousin who built my first shelf?
fixed.scene_if_held: Bram. I can smell the sawdust from here. Thank you for holding that.

wren.reason: Good character detail (sawdust, the shelf). Held scene made less vague.

draft.told: I only drink a blend called 'Mist and Mint'. Anything else tastes like forgetting.
draft.ask_later: What is the specific name of my tea?
draft.scene_if_held: The cup feels full again, not just with liquid.

fixed.told: My favourite tea is a blend called "Mist and Mint". Tansy says it is not strictly a real blend, but she makes it for me anyway.
fixed.ask_later: What is the name of my favourite tea blend?
fixed.scene_if_held: Mist and Mint. The cup feels fuller already.

wren.reason: Fine, but "anything else tastes like forgetting" is a little dark, and Tansy sells rosemary tea on the Quay, so Wren's tea is made a favourite rather than her only one. Three of the drafts are about food or drink, so use only one or two in a run.

draft.title: Wick Trimming Rule

Dip not past the knot line
Smoke rises when oil runs dry

River barges carry amber jars

fixed.title: Wick Trimming Rule
lines: Clip the cotton fringe low
Dip no deeper than the knot line
Smoke rises when the oil runs dry
Keep spare wicks in the fox tin
Trim again at the first bell

tablets.reason: Rule-style lines, a good tablet. Lines 4 and 5 do not belong to a wick rule (a fox, amber jars) and would confuse the picture. Rewritten to stay on topic.

draft.title: The River Ferry Rule

Sleeping fish beneath the hulls

tablets.reason: Too close to the shipped "The Night Ferry" tablet (boat, mist, lanterns, dock). Lines are descriptions, not rules, and the title says "Rule".

lines: Knead the flour with river water first
Crack 3 eggs into the clay bowl
Sprinkle sea salt before it rises
Let the loaf cool beside the window
Pour wild honey over the golden crust

tablets.reason: A good, concrete tablet. Line 3 (a fox smelling bread) is odd. Number written as a digit, as the exact-match rule in TABLETS_V requires.
